codex.detail: The Codex lens process was launched but had not produced a usable artifact before synthesis time.

copilot.detail: The Copilot lens wrote process narration but not a completed structured result.

devilsAdvocate.detail: Returned a usable JSON lens result emphasizing that wake hint and durable review/ack semantics must stay separate.

candidateDirections.name: Crews MCP wake plus native Codex queued-input bridge
candidateDirections.summary: Keep the existing crews mailbox/review cursor as source of truth, add a tiny crews MCP notification source for mailbox writes, and add a Codex-native next-turn queue bridge so specific crews notifications become queued prompts without a listener subprocess.

candidateDirections.name: Route crews delivery through happy-cli instead of raw codex
candidateDirections.summary: Reuse the already-shipped happy-cli MCP notification consumer and durable mailbox wake pattern by changing the runtime architecture so crews codex sessions run through happy-cli's codex wrapper.

candidateDirections.name: Keep the listener subprocess and surface its completion better
candidateDirections.summary: Use the existing BackgroundProcessNotification wake path to make listener exits show up more naturally in codex, but keep the listener/review-mail loop intact.

recommendedDirection.name: Crews MCP wake plus native Codex queued-input bridge
recommendedDirection.summary: The best listener-less shape is to copy the happy agent-comms split: durable mailbox remains authoritative, MCP resource_updated is only a wake hint, and native Codex injects a queued next-turn prompt by reusing the existing input-queue wake pattern rather than relying on the current happy-cli-only Option B consumer.
why: Mailbox writes, not process exits, are the right producer event for crews mail; BackgroundProcessNotification only models subprocess completion.

The already-merged MCP notification ingress is real, but in raw Codex it stops at EventMsg::McpServerNotification and does not become model-visible queued input; that is why a small new codex fork patch is still required.
Keeping review/ack semantics explicit avoids splitting truth between transcript text and .crews mailbox history.

chosenCodexSeam.reason: These are the existing native Codex primitives that queue next-turn ResponseInputItems and wake pending work. A crews-specific MCP notification consumer should reuse this exact mechanism so mail is delivered between turns in the same way background shell completion is already delivered today.

mcpNotificationIngress.finding: Codex can already ingest MCP server notifications and emit EventMsg::McpServerNotification, but raw Codex does not yet turn that event into queued model input.

rawCodexNativeGap.finding: Raw Codex currently ignores EventMsg::McpServerNotification in the native turn path.

happyCliOptionB.finding: The existing prompt-queue consumer is in happy-cli, not in plain crews-spawned Codex sessions.

backgroundProcessNotification.finding: This already queues a synthetic next-turn message and wakes pending work, but only for subprocess exits; it does not model mailbox writes and still assumes a listener subprocess exists.

agentCommsPattern.finding: The durable-mailbox plus resource_updated wake split already solves 'wake is hint, mailbox is truth' and includes startup catch-up semantics.

crewsSideChanges: Add a small Codex-visible MCP surface for crews mail. The current crews codex plugin manifest has hooks only and no mcpServers entry (`ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\.codex-plugin\plugin.json:1-18`, `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\.codex-plugin\hooks\hooks.json:1-60`).

Keep `.crews` mailbox files and review cursors as the source of truth. A wake notification must never mark mail reviewed; only the existing review-mail/markReviewed path should advance `lastReviewedSeq` (`ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\hooks\commands\review-mail.js:220-298`, `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\hooks\actors.js:1454-1473`).

Emit resource_updated (or equivalent MCP server notification) on mailbox writes, keyed by actor/session identity, and reuse existing review-mail formatting rather than inventing a second mailbox schema.
Add startup catch-up for codex sessions: if `lastReviewRequiredSeq > lastReviewedSeq`, inject one wake hint on SessionStart the same way happy agent-comms recovery enqueues one wake on startup.
codexSideChanges: Add a small native consumer for crews-tagged MCP notifications that synthesizes one queued next-turn prompt using the existing `queue_response_items_for_next_turn(...)` + `request_pending_work_wake()` pattern (`core\src\session\input_queue.rs:82-88`, `core\src\unified_exec\async_watcher.rs:184-188`).

Do not rely on the current happy-cli Option B consumer for raw codex sessions; that consumer only exists in `packages\happy-cli\src\codex\mcpNotificationConsumer.ts` and is not present in plain codex TUI flows.
Gate the new behavior narrowly, ideally by MCP server name plus notification kind, so generic MCP notifications continue to behave as Stage A event-only traffic.
Preserve 'between turns only' semantics; the new path should queue input for the next turn, not preempt an active LLM call.

codex.preToolUse: Replace the listener-arm-first requirement with a codex-specific 'notification bridge healthy' requirement. Once the bridge is active, the unarmed review-mail-first block at `ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\hooks\pre-tool-use.js:590-635` should not fire for codex actors.
codex.stop: Relax the listener-armed end-of-turn requirement only for codex actors that have the bridge enabled. Keep review-required and strict-ack behavior unchanged; only the reachability primitive changes.
codex.reviewFlow: The wake prompt should tell the actor to run review-mail (or a future equivalent drain tool/resource). The wake itself is not the ack path.

claudeCopilot.behavior: Keep the current listener model unchanged, including the review-mail-first block and the lead/member listener gates.

conflictSurface.summary: Listener-less delivery for plain crews-spawned codex sessions cannot ride only already-merged seams. The producer half is missing in crews, and the native consumer half is missing in raw Codex.
whyNotAlreadyMergedOnly: Current Stage A MCP notification ingress stops at EventMsg::McpServerNotification in raw Codex (`core\src\session\turn.rs:1370-1371`).
The shipped prompt-queue consumer lives only in happy-cli (`packages\happy-cli\src\codex\runCodex.ts:299-313`, `:766-775`).
The crews codex plugin today exposes only hooks, not an MCP server (`ai-developer-toolkit\plugins\crews\.codex-plugin\plugin.json:1-18`).

upstreamConflictDelta.crewsPlugin: low - plugin-local new files plus codex plugin manifest wiring
upstreamConflictDelta.codexFork: medium - a new native notification-to-input bridge is needed, but it can reuse existing queue/wake primitives and should be implementable with mostly new files and a small seam
upstreamConflictDelta.happyCli: optional/low - useful as prior art or a fallback architecture, but not required for the recommended direct-codex path

leadApplicability.currentCopilotLead: Limited direct benefit. Copilot already has its own system_notification/background-task wake path, so this does not unify today's lead runtime.
leadApplicability.codexMembers: High benefit. This is the primary target: no listener-arm loop, async wake on mailbox writes, explicit review/ack preserved.
leadApplicability.futureCodexLead: Also high benefit. The same bridge can replace the current codex-specific listener gates for a codex lead once that runtime exists.

fallbackIfNoNewCodexPatch.summary: Keep the existing listener subprocess and use BackgroundProcessNotification to surface its exit/completion more naturally.
fallbackIfNoNewCodexPatch.tradeoff: Lowest conflict, but it does not remove the listener loop and does not solve the operator's listener-less goal.

followUpPlan.shape: One plan spanning two implementation surfaces: (1) crews plugin adds a codex MCP wake source over the existing mailbox, (2) codex fork adds a narrow native notification-to-next-turn queue bridge, (3) crews hook gates branch on 'listener or codex bridge reachable'.
stories: Story 1: crews codex MCP wake source and startup catch-up
Story 3: codex-only hook-gate relaxation and smoke coverage
